rows: 1. Gestational Age Limit & Number of RMP Opinions Required

• Up to 12 weeks: Opinion of 1 RMP.
• 12 to 20 weeks: Opinion of 2 RMPs.
• Beyond 20 weeks: Not permitted (except to immediately save the woman’s life).

• Up to 20 weeks: Opinion of 1 Registered Medical Practitioner (RMP).
• 20 to 24 weeks: Opinion of 2 RMPs (for specified vulnerable categories of women).
• Beyond 24 weeks: Permitted for substantial fetal abnormalities diagnosed by a State-level Medical Board [1, 2].

Extended to “any woman or her partner” (up to 20 weeks), thereby legally empowering unmarried / single women to access safe abortion for contraceptive failure [1, 2].

Upper ceiling was strictly 20 weeks for all categories.

Extended up to 24 weeks for 7 special categories:
1. Survivors of sexual assault, rape, or incest.
2. Minors.
3. Change of marital status during the ongoing pregnancy (widowhood or divorce).
4. Women with physical disabilities (major disability under RPwD Act, 2016).
5. Mentally ill women (including mental retardation).
6. Fetal malformation incompatible with life or causing serious handicap.
7. Women in humanitarian settings, disaster, or emergency situations declared by the Government [1, 2].
